newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England signals no rate change this month.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England signals no rate change this month.

text.p: The Bank of England left official interest rates unchanged on Wednesday after the monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
The Bank set an unchanged repo rate of 6.0 percent for its routine money market operations at 1430 GMT, having done precisely the same thing at midday, just after the monetary meeting broke up.
Clarke sets interest rates after taking advice from the Bank of England, but the central bank normally makes no formal announcement if rates are left unchanged.
George has recently been pressing for a rise of a quarter of a percentage point in interest rates because he fears a resurgence in inflation.
But Clarke, whose Conservative government faces an election in the next two months, has rejected his advice, arguing that there is no clear evidence that the economy is about to overheat.
Clarke has a strong political incentive not to raise rates before the election as this would mean dearer home loans for millions of Britons.

Financial markets had been left uncertain after the Bank's first round of money market operations on Wednesday. This came so soon after Clarke's meeting with George ended that no-one was sure whether Bank officials were simply waiting for the next round of operations before acting.
